audit_findings.title: Stale cash and share dates could double-count buyback value
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.8 million demonstrated through June 9, 2026, approximately $0.29 per diluted share; post-June 9 activity unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds May 2 cash while the share denominator reflects subsequent repurchases, counting the repurchase capital in cash and again through fewer shares.
audit_findings.evidence: From the end of fiscal 2025 through April 14, 2026, the Company utilized $10.7 million to repurchase 231,153 shares under the stock buyback program, leaving $51.0 million available under the September 2024 Stock Repurchase Program.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date mismatch. The known $3.8 million would reduce intrinsic value by about $0.29 per share, small against the $5.59 gap between the $35.02 buy-below level and the $29.43 price. However, repurchases, dividends, awards and cash movements from June 9 through September 6 are not reconciled, so the total valuation-date error and its materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Roll forward cash, restricted cash and fully diluted shares from May 2 through September 6 using repurchase settlements, dividends and equity-award activity, then rerun the bridge on one common date.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may precede a material tariff margin reset
audit_findings.mechanism: Unmitigated tariffs would raise cost of sales and reduce recurring owner earnings and potentially sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Specifically, the latest tariffs implemented by the U.S. would have significant impact on our cost structure and product margins.
audit_findings.explanation: No anchor error is demonstrated. The first-quarter filing confirms continuing tariff exposure but also reports pricing benefits and a $10.4 million tariff-refund benefit, including $7.0 million related to prior-year costs. Those refund amounts do not quantify the recurring burden from newly implemented tariffs. The possible margin reset is therefore forward-looking and not presently measurable from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Track tariff-inclusive inventory through subsequent cost of sales and compare gross margin excluding refunds with pricing, unit demand and sourcing mitigation; rerun the OE scenarios if a recurring net burden emerges.

audit_findings.title: Gift-card breakage makes the anchor estimate-sensitive
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.2 million FY2026 breakage revenue; $1.3 million revenue sensitivity to a hypothetical 1% breakage-rate change
audit_findings.mechanism: An excessive breakage estimate increases revenue, net income and the latest-actual OE anchor, which is capitalized throughout the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Auditing the Company’s breakage revenue related to unredeemed gift cards was complex and judgmental due to the complexity of the model and the subjectivity related to the judgments that are made by the Company to estimate the breakage rate.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved estimation risk, not a demonstrated accounting error. Breakage revenue equals 13.9% of the $44.7 million anchor. As a conservative scale test, removing the full $6.2 million dollar-for-dollar from OE would lower the base buy-below level by about $4.67 per share, from $35.02 to approximately $30.35, leaving only about $0.92 over the $29.43 market price. The issue is therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion when combined with ordinary estimation or tax effects.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cohort redemption data, the fourth-quarter breakage-rate calculation and post-year-end adjustments; quantify the supported after-tax OE normalization and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $25.843 million, approximately $1.98 intrinsic value per share or $1.38 per share at the 30% margin of safety
audit_findings.mechanism: Minimum operating cash belongs inside the operating business and should be excluded from the separable cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash requirements are primarily for the opening, remodeling or reformatting of stores, installation and upgrades of information systems and working capital.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, but even treating none of the $25.843 million as excess would reduce the base buy-below level only from $35.02 to approximately $33.64. That remains $4.21 above the $29.43 market price, so this finding alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating cash from seasonal troughs, working-capital requirements, committed capital spending and credit availability, then add only the verified excess amount to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring currency gain may remain in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.8 million, 4.0% of anchor OE; maximum computed base buy-below impact approximately $1.35 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If unadjusted, the SGA currency gain increases net-income-based OE and therefore the anchor, forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded a gain of $ 1.8 million i n fiscal 2025 , and loss of $ 0.2 million and $ 0.1 million related to foreign currency in fisc al 2024 and 2023 , r espectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE schedule already normalized the gain is unresolved. Nevertheless, conservatively removing the entire $1.8 million dollar-for-dollar from the $44.7 million anchor would lower the base buy-below level from $35.02 to approximately $33.67, still $4.24 above the $29.43 price. The after-tax effect would be smaller, so the finding is not material to the conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2026 OE reconciliation for a currency adjustment; if absent, separate ordinary transaction exposure from the nonrepeatable gain and rerun using the supported after-tax amount.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation obligations require a net claim check
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded deferred-compensation obligation not represented in forecast OE is a claim ahead of common equity and belongs as a net deduction in the equity bridge after matching dedicated assets.
audit_findings.evidence: We have various contractual or other obligations, including operating lease commitments and obligations under deferred compensation plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings identify $1.322 million of deferred-compensation assets at May 2, 2026 but do not separately disclose the corresponding plan obligation or establish whether it is fully funded and already captured elsewhere. No omitted net liability is demonstrated, and the record cannot establish its scale or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the plan obligation and asset statements, identify where the liability is recorded, reconcile current and noncurrent balances, and rerun the bridge only for any verified unfunded amount not captured in OE.
